question: What is the main difference between an acute kidney injury and chronic renal failure?

options.A: Chronic renal failure always resolves completely with proper hydration therapy.
options.B: Acute injury develops slowly over several years without causing any symptoms.
options.C: Acute injury only affects the bladder, while chronic failure affects the entire ureter.
options.D: Chronic renal failure involves permanent and irreversible loss of nephron function.

explanation: You've got this! Chronic renal failure causes permanent scarring and loss of nephrons over time. Acute injury, on the other hand, can often be reversed if caught early. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T7#GNS213_U4_T7_h1)

question: Why do the remaining healthy nephrons get larger (hypertrophy) during the early stages of chronic kidney disease?

options.A: To produce extra urine that completely flushes out all uremic toxins from the body
options.B: To increase blood pressure so that the heart pumps faster to the extremities
options.C: To compensate for the workload of the nephrons that have already been destroyed
options.D: To store extra electrolytes and vitamins for future metabolic needs

explanation: Think of it like a team picking up extra shifts when coworkers drop out. Healthy nephrons try to take over the filtering work, but this extra strain eventually causes them to burn out too. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T7#GNS213_U4_T7_h1)

question: What is the single most common cause of chronic renal failure here in Nigeria?
explanation: Great clinical insight to carry into practice! High blood pressure puts constant, hard pressure on the tiny blood vessels in the kidneys, making it the leading cause of renal failure in our region. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T7#GNS213_U4_T7_h2)

question: How do unregulated herbal remedies often contribute to chronic kidney disease in clinical practice?

options.A: By lowering systemic blood pressure so drastically that blood stops flowing
options.B: By stimulating the overproduction of red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.C: By causing sudden dehydration that increases daily urine output permanently
options.D: By introducing heavy metals and toxic substances that damage the kidney tubules

explanation: As nurses, we see this often. Many traditional concoctions contain hidden toxins that gradually injure the delicate filtering structures of the kidneys over long periods of use. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T7#GNS213_U4_T7_h2)

question: Why do patients with chronic renal failure frequently look very pale and complain of severe tiredness?

options.A: The liver stops producing enough protein to carry vitamins.
options.B: Decreased erythropoietin production leads to anemia.
options.C: Excess sodium in the blood blocks oxygen from entering the lungs.
options.D: High potassium levels destroy red blood cells in the bloodstream.

explanation: Remember, damaged kidneys forget to make enough erythropoietin—the hormone that tells your bone marrow to build red blood cells. Without it, anemia sets in! [learn more](GNS213_U4_T7#GNS213_U4_T7_h3)

question: A patient with end-stage kidney disease complains of severe itching all over their body. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: An allergic reaction to the standard hospital soap used during morning care
options.B: Mineral imbalances causing calcium-phosphate crystals to deposit in the skin tissues
options.C: Excessive production of red blood cells causing severe pressure under the skin
options.D: A sudden viral skin infection caused by a weakened immune system

explanation: Poor kidneys struggle to balance calcium and phosphorus. When phosphorus builds up, tiny mineral crystals form under the skin, causing that intense, frustrating itch. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T7#GNS213_U4_T7_h3)

question: What is considered the best overall laboratory test to check how well the kidneys are working?
explanation: You'll see eGFR results on patient charts every day. It estimates how fast your glomeruli are filtering blood using creatinine levels, making it the gold standard for kidney function. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T7#GNS213_U4_T7_h4)

question: Why is finding protein persistently in a patient's urine an important warning sign?

options.A: It confirms that the liver is failing to process dietary nutrients properly.
options.B: It shows that the bladder is contracting too frequently during the day.
options.C: It indicates that the filtering barriers of the glomeruli have been damaged.
options.D: It proves that the patient is eating too much protein in their daily diet.

explanation: Healthy glomeruli act like a strict bouncer, keeping big protein molecules safely inside the blood. If protein leaks into the urine, it tells us those filters are injured. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T7#GNS213_U4_T7_h4)

question: Why are ACE inhibitor medications often given to kidney disease patients even if their blood pressure is completely normal?

options.A: They stimulate the bone marrow to produce extra white blood cells.
options.B: They absorb extra phosphorus directly from the gastrointestinal tract.
options.C: They reduce pressure inside the glomeruli and decrease protein leakage.
options.D: They dissolve calcium deposits that form inside the renal tubules.

explanation: Think of ACE inhibitors as pressure-relieving valves for the nephrons. By easing the internal filtering pressure, they protect the kidneys from wearing out faster. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T7#GNS213_U4_T7_h5)

question: What is the main goal of giving 'phosphate binders' to a patient with kidney failure?

options.A: To lower systemic blood pressure by relaxing blood vessel walls
options.B: To prevent dietary phosphorus from being absorbed in the gut
options.C: To increase daily urine output and reduce swelling in the legs
options.D: To stimulate red blood cell production in the bone marrow

explanation: Patients take these binders right with their meals. The medicine grabs onto phosphorus in the food and carries it out safely through the stool so it doesn't flood the blood. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T7#GNS213_U4_T7_h5)

question: During peritoneal dialysis, what part of the patient's body acts as the natural filtering membrane?

options.A: The peritoneal membrane inside the abdominal cavity
options.B: The inner lining of the urinary bladder walls
options.C: The basement membrane of the remaining renal tubules
options.D: The semipermeable filter inside the hemodialysis machine

explanation: Peritoneal dialysis is clever! It uses the patient's own rich network of blood vessels inside the abdominal lining (the peritoneum) to filter out waste and extra water. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T7#GNS213_U4_T7_h6)

question: What is a major, non-negotiable requirement for a patient who has received a successful kidney transplant?

options.A: Avoiding all forms of physical activity to protect the new incision site
options.B: Undergoing hemodialysis twice a week to clean the transplanted organ
options.C: Following a strict low-protein diet for the rest of their natural life
options.D: Taking lifelong immunosuppressive medications to prevent organ rejection

explanation: The body's immune system naturally views a new organ as a stranger and tries to fight it. Transplant patients must take anti-rejection drugs every single day to protect their new kidney. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T7#GNS213_U4_T7_h6)

question: You are assessing a patient with a newly created AV fistula in their arm. What finding tells you it is open and working well?

options.A: A palpable thrill and audible bruit over the fistula site
options.B: Absence of any sound or vibration when listening with a stethoscope
options.C: A cool hand with weak pulses past the surgical site
options.D: A strong pulse with severe pain and redness in the fingers

explanation: You'll love listening for this in the ward! When arterial and venous blood rush together, it creates a gentle vibration (thrill) and a swishing sound (bruit) that confirms good blood flow. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T7#GNS213_U4_T7_h7)

question: Why is stepping on the scale to check daily body weight so crucial in the care plan for kidney failure?

options.A: It measures how well the bone marrow is producing red blood cells.
options.B: It helps calculate the exact amount of protein the patient needs to eat.
options.C: It is the most sensitive daily indicator of fluid retention or loss.
options.D: It indicates whether the patient is taking their iron supplements on time.

explanation: Numbers don't lie! A sudden weight gain over a day or two almost always means the kidneys are struggling and the body is holding onto dangerous amounts of fluid. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T7#GNS213_U4_T7_h7)
